About AI discoveries in 2022

This selection contains 421 catalog entries dated 4 Jan 2022 to 30 Dec 2022. 421 include structured evidence annotations describing reported tests, the AI contribution and remaining limits. Missing annotations mean those details have not been structured here, not that a study lacks evidence.

Dates follow the catalog publication policy. Coverage is selected and incomplete; entries can overlap or describe several results. Counts do not measure independent discoveries, clinical benefit or worldwide research output. Read the selection and evidence policy or compare catalog coverage by year and field.

29 Dec 2022Nihon University School of Medicine

Deep-learning chest-radiograph pressure estimates associate with heart-failure prognosis

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A post hoc analysis of 534 acute-heart-failure admissions applied a previously developed VGG16-based model to estimate pulmonary arterial wedge pressure from chest radiographs. Higher discharge estimates and smaller decreases during hospitalization were associated with death or heart-failure readmission after adjustment; 223 patients reached the composite endpoint. This single-centre observational analysis does not establish a causal treatment target or improved care. Imaging-view differences and exclusion of in-hospital deaths limit interpretation.

Technology: VGG16-based regression convolutional neural network

Editorial relevance 40 medicine Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Previously trained VGG16 regression CNN with global-average-pooling output estimates pressure; model trained on 748 and tested on 188 data in earlier study. Present post hoc 534-patient registry links estimated pressure to outcomes; original prospective registry collection does not establish frozen-model prospective validation.
Test and result
Retrospective admission/discharge imaging and adjusted outcome association over median 289 days follow-up.
Limitation / still unknown
Prospective clinical utility, multicentre transportability and equivalence across radiograph views remain unestablished.

29 Dec 2022University of Urbino Carlo Bo; Istituto Auxologico Italiano; University of Milano-Bicocca; University of Bologna; University of L’Aquila; University of Brescia

Retrospective screening study measures the sensitivity–specificity trade-off of learned hypertension detection

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A random-forest model evaluated on a held-out subset of an Italian blood-pressure screening campaign identified previously unrecognized high blood pressure with a different sensitivity–specificity trade-off from a simple risk-factor protocol. The endpoint was same-visit elevated blood pressure, not future hypertension. Results were modest and did not establish cost savings, better patient outcomes or universal superiority over clinical screening.

Technology: Random forest classification with training-set undersampling

Editorial relevance 40 medicine Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The learned RF combined questionnaire and demographic predictors to classify measured previously unrecognized elevated blood pressure, enabling a specific retrospective clinical-screening validation and its observed sensitivity–specificity trade-off.
Test and result
From 37,110 campaign participants in 2015–2019, the analysis retained 20,206 adults without known or treated hypertension, including 4,192 newly detected cases defined by measured blood pressure. Data were randomly split into 14,144 training and 6,062 validation records; hyperparameter search used training cross-validation and resampling was applied to training data. The selected undersampled random forest reported sensitivity 0.818, specificity 0.629 and AUC 0.816.
Limitation / still unknown
Volunteer participation, complete-case exclusions, self-reported predictors and same-visit blood-pressure labeling limit interpretation. The clinical risk-factor comparator was applied to the original dataset, while model performance used the validation subset; this is not a paired matched-set intervention comparison. Models/configurations were compared on one internal validation cohort, without independent geographic/temporal replication. Single-visit elevated pressure does not establish future onset or longitudinal clinical diagnosis.

28 Dec 2022Johns Hopkins University; Dartmouth College

Learned brain patterns link pain ratings and cognitive measures

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A machine-learning mediation analysis identified brain patterns jointly related to heat intensity and pain ratings, and connectivity patterns related to fluid intelligence and working-memory accuracy. The December 2022 journal analysis used existing fMRI datasets; a related preprint appeared in October 2022. The authors explicitly avoid causal interpretation.

Technology: 3D convolutional neural network and ridge-regression connectome predictive modeling

Editorial relevance 33 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
A fitted CNN compressed activation maps into learned mediators optimized through the path model; ridge-regression connectome modeling supplied the second application. Conventional path analysis and bootstrapping tested the resulting associations.
Test and result
Pain models used 209 training participants across seven studies and a 75-person eighth-study evaluation, with activation patterns related to heat intensity and pain ratings. The pain-model association was absent for aversive sound trials in that evaluation; leave-study-out mediation was significant for five of eight pain datasets. A separate HCP analysis used 558 training and 240 test participants, identifying connectivity patterns jointly related to fluid intelligence and working-memory accuracy.
Limitation / still unknown
These are statistical mediation associations, not established neural causal pathways. Training Methods explicitly evaluated iteration-specific mediation on test data and selected the most stable indirect effect; those test results are therefore not a wholly untouched final confirmation. The pain data had previously been analyzed with a different mediation method, and familiar pain regions were recovered alongside exploratory differences. SHAP localization and its arbitrary threshold do not establish independent biological mechanisms. The primary preprint API dates version1 to October 11, 2022, but its full result tables were not read; journal-specific claims are not assigned that earlier date. The HCP split is within one source cohort, not a separate independently collected cohort.

Integrated proteomics and metabolomics with LASSO nominate a four-analyte early IgA-nephropathy plasma panel

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A study of biopsy-confirmed IgA nephropathy (IgAN) integrated plasma proteomics and untargeted metabolomics and used LASSO logistic regression to select PRKAR2A, IL6ST, SOS1 and palmitoleic acid as candidate discriminators from healthy controls. The panel had AUC 0.994 in the training set and 0.977 in the test split; ELISA assays in a separate 9-case/10-control sample set yielded an AUC of 0.91. Proteomic and metabolomic analyses also indicated complement/immune activation and altered energy and amino-acid metabolism in the studied cases.

Technology: LASSO logistic regression (glmnet), with tenfold cross-validation and additional random-forest/SVM model checks

Editorial relevance 53 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
LASSO feature selection on integrated proteomic and metabolomic measurements nominated the four-analyte panel; the study evaluated its classification in a held-out split and measured the selected analytes by ELISA in an independent sample batch.
Test and result
A study of biopsy-confirmed IgA nephropathy (IgAN) integrated plasma proteomics and untargeted metabolomics and used LASSO logistic regression to select PRKAR2A, IL6ST, SOS1 and palmitoleic acid as candidate discriminators from healthy controls.
Limitation / still unknown
This is an early candidate biomarker result, not a validated clinical test or biopsy replacement. The discovery analysis included 33 biopsy-confirmed IgAN cases and 20 healthy controls; the separate ELISA group contained only 9 IgAN cases and 10 controls from the same hospital. The test split is small, and the study did not test specificity against other kidney diseases or demonstrate prospective/clinical utility. The proposed biomarker biology remains speculative.

Machine-learning-guided electrochemical screening isolates five new reaction products

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A machine-learning-guided, chemist-in-the-loop screen predicted electrochemical reactivity for 38,865 potential partners with 1,4-dicyanobenzene (DCB). Automated tests of 20 prioritized, previously untested partners yielded DCB conversion in 16; five produced an isolable major product judged of synthetic or mechanistic interest. The reported examples include a silyl-enol-ether coupling and electrochemical benzylic arylation of benzyltrimethylsilane with DCB, plus three mechanistically unexpected products.

Technology: Machine-learning-guided reaction-competency classifier using a DFT-informed molecular representation

Editorial relevance 60 chemistry Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The model screened a 38,865-member virtual set for reaction competency and, with chemist selection, prioritized 20 new partners for automated electrolysis. The experiments measured DCB conversion, then product analysis isolated and characterized five major products from the selected set.
Test and result
Automated tests of 20 prioritized, previously untested partners yielded DCB conversion in 16; five produced an isolable major product judged of synthetic or mechanistic interest.
Limitation / still unknown
This is an early reaction-discovery demonstration under one fixed DCB electrolysis system, not a general reaction predictor or optimized synthetic platform. Seven of the 16 DCB-converting selected reactions gave complex mixtures without an appreciable single isolated product; five yielded isolable major products, reported at low yields and without method optimization. DCB conversion alone does not establish a product identity, and the three mechanistically ambiguous outcomes require further study.

14 Dec 2022Columbia University; ETH Zurich; Swiss Federal Institute for Forest, Snow and Landscape Research (WSL)

Unsupervised seismic clustering reveals distinct drainage signals at Gornergletscher

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: An unsupervised analysis of five weeks of seismic records from Gornergletscher, Switzerland, separated cryoseismic signals into clusters associated with the 2007 Gornersee lake flood and with afternoon/evening meltwater flow. One high-energy, broadband noise cluster began about two days before the reported onset of subglacial flooding; the authors suggest it captures the earlier initiation of englacial and subglacial drainage and improves the flood chronology.

Technology: SpecUFEx unsupervised feature extraction: non-negative matrix factorization, hidden Markov modeling, principal component analysis, and k-means clustering

Editorial relevance 47 physics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The unsupervised learning pipeline reduced seismic spectrograms to fingerprints and grouped similar continuous-noise and icequake signals without labels. Comparing the learned clusters with lake level, GPS, temperature, and event timing exposed distinct clusters associated with lake-flood drainage and daily meltwater flow, which supported the revised drainage chronology.
Test and result
An unsupervised analysis of five weeks of seismic records from Gornergletscher, Switzerland, separated cryoseismic signals into clusters associated with the 2007 Gornersee lake flood and with afternoon/evening meltwater flow.
Limitation / still unknown
The analysis covers five weeks at one glacier using the 2007 flood record. The inferred drainage start precedes lake-level evidence by about two days, but the source cannot definitively exclude ice-bed slip, till deformation, or small fractures as explanations for some spectral features. The study interprets cluster timing and spectra as hydrologic signals; it does not directly image subglacial drainage pathways.

29 Nov 2022Jinan University; Shenzhen People’s Hospital; collaborating institutions

Machine-learning-guided PBMC proteomics identifies SLE diagnosis and activity biomarker panels

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A random-forest and OPLS-DA prioritization pipeline applied to peripheral-blood mononuclear-cell proteomics identified candidate protein combinations for distinguishing systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) from healthy and rheumatoid-arthritis controls and for separating active from inactive SLE. ELISA in a separate 80-person cohort supported a six-protein diagnosis panel (IFIT3, MX1, TOMM40, STAT1, STAT2 and OAS3; AUC 0.723 versus healthy controls and 0.815 versus rheumatoid arthritis) and a nine-protein activity panel (AUC 0.990). Single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis mapped several associated interferon-signature proteins to specific immune-cell populations.

Technology: POC-SLE: random-forest feature ranking with 1,000 bootstrap iterations, combined with OPLS-DA variable-importance selection

Editorial relevance 60 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The random forest ranked differentially expressed proteins from discovery-cohort PBMC proteomics; its selected proteins were intersected with OPLS-DA features to construct candidate diagnosis and activity panels. Researchers evaluated those panels with ELISA in a separate cohort and used single-cell transcriptomic data to examine immune-cell sources.
Test and result
ELISA in a separate 80-person cohort supported a six-protein diagnosis panel (IFIT3, MX1, TOMM40, STAT1, STAT2 and OAS3; AUC 0.723 versus healthy controls and 0.815 versus rheumatoid arthritis) and a nine-protein activity panel (AUC 0.990).
Limitation / still unknown
The study is cross-sectional and the ELISA validation cohort contained 80 people from the same clinical setting; it does not establish longitudinal flare prediction, treatment response, causal mechanisms or clinical utility. The six-protein panel had moderate discrimination versus healthy controls (AUC 0.723) and better but still cohort-specific discrimination versus rheumatoid arthritis (AUC 0.815). The activity-panel AUC of 0.990 was reported for active versus inactive groups in this validation cohort and needs broader independent validation. Authors note limited sample size/ethnic diversity and need for mechanistic study.

Autonomous microscopy discovers an edge plasmon in layered MnPS₃

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Deep-kernel-learning-guided STEM-EELS measurements identified a low-energy edge-localized plasmon response in the layered antiferromagnet MnPS₃, distinct from the higher-energy bulk plasmon response. The system used local structure to predict spectra and uncertainty, then autonomously selected where to measure based on a physics-defined objective. After 10–25 spectra, about 1% of the image-space points, it localized the edge mode to the flake boundary.

Technology: Deep kernel learning (feed-forward neural-network feature embedding with a Gaussian-process kernel and physics-based acquisition/scalarizer)

Editorial relevance 53 physics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The model learned a structure-to-electron-energy-loss-spectrum relationship from sequential measurements and used its predicted response and uncertainty to choose subsequent STEM probe locations. A user-specified spectral scalarizer prioritized a low-energy feature relative to the bulk plasmon; the closed-loop instrument then discovered and mapped an edge-localized response without pretraining on MnPS₃ sample data.
Test and result
Deep-kernel-learning-guided STEM-EELS measurements identified a low-energy edge-localized plasmon response in the layered antiferromagnet MnPS₃, distinct from the higher-energy bulk plasmon response.
Limitation / still unknown
The paper demonstrates the mode in the reported exfoliated MnPS₃ flake and STEM-EELS setup. The physical search objective was supplied by researchers (a spectral feature below the bulk-plasmon peak), so the AI did not independently formulate the scientific question. The authors report that the edge response varied with local boundary shape and present this as a proof-of-concept discovery workflow, not a complete theory of MnPS₃ plasmon behavior.

4 Nov 2022Oak Ridge National Laboratory; Argonne National Laboratory; Instituto de Física de Líquidos y Sistemas Biológicos, UNLP-CONICET

Machine-learning-assisted neutron scattering shows hydrostatic pressure tunes interactions in spin ice

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Machine-learning-assisted analysis of diffuse neutron scattering from Dy₂Ti₂O₇ at ambient pressure and about 1.3 GPa extracted pressure-dependent Hamiltonian parameters and found that hydrostatic pressure modifies further-neighbor magnetic interactions and the material’s nanoscale magnetic-glass ordering. The analysis supports using pressure to tune the spin-ice glass state. A transition at substantially higher pressure is a model-based prediction, not an observed transition in this experiment.

Technology: Nonlinear autoencoder, radial-basis generative surrogate and hierarchical clustering for neutron-scattering analysis

Editorial relevance 53 materials Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The nonlinear autoencoder compressed measured and simulated diffuse neutron-scattering volumes; a trained generative surrogate enabled fast forward prediction of scattering from spin-Hamiltonian parameters, while clustering and inverse mapping constrained parameters against the experiment. Those ML components made it practical to analyze pressure-dependent measurements and infer the change in further-neighbor couplings during the neutron experiment workflow.
Test and result
Machine-learning-assisted analysis of diffuse neutron scattering from Dy₂Ti₂O₇ at ambient pressure and about 1.3 GPa extracted pressure-dependent Hamiltonian parameters and found that hydrostatic pressure modifies further-neighbor magnetic interactions and the material’s nanoscale magnetic-glass ordering.
Limitation / still unknown
The reported pressure comparison is between ambient pressure and an estimated hydrostatic pressure of about 1.3 GPa, using separate measurement setups. The change in magnetic couplings and glass morphology is inferred by fitting a spin model to scattering with ML-assisted analysis, not measured as a direct microscopic coupling. The authors predict that substantially higher pressure may induce a phase transition; no such transition was observed here. Some analysis and experimental steering remained manual.

Test and result
The source derived 541,354 procedure records from 392,661 patients, using prior diagnosis/medication windows and coded VTE within thirty days. A 70:30 random procedure split evaluated a six-hidden-layer DNN. Final Table 6 reports AUC 0.901 after genetic feature selection versus 0.780 using established risk factors. The abstract instead cites 0.873, which main text assigns to a preliminary feature-selection stage.
Limitation / still unknown
Patients could contribute multiple procedures, and patient-level partition isolation was not established. Broad procedure-code ranges may include operations beyond hip/knee replacement. Genetic selection/tuning isolation from final evaluation remains unclear; excluding postoperative prophylaxis also limits preoperative applicability. The Table6/abstract difference is not silently resolved. Drug-feature importance is associational and does not establish medication harms or benefit from changing treatment.

2 Oct 2022Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg; University of Coimbra; Friedrich Schiller University Jena

Crystal-graph learning and DFT identify 19,512 additional thermodynamically stable materials

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: The authors trained crystal-graph attention networks on an expanded, composition- and symmetry-balanced dataset and used them to search 2,500 binary and ternary structure prototypes covering about one billion inorganic compounds. Density-functional-theory validation identified 19,512 additional compounds on the calculated thermodynamic convex hull and about 150,000 more within 50 meV/atom of it; the paper also analyzed predicted superconducting and superhard materials and compounds with large gap deformation potentials.

Technology: Crystal-graph attention neural networks trained on expanded density-functional-theory materials data

AI contribution
The graph networks accelerated screening of roughly one billion prototype-generated candidates, after which density-functional-theory calculations validated stability for identified candidates; machine learning plus ab initio calculations also ranked materials for selected functional properties.
Test and result
The authors trained crystal-graph attention networks on an expanded, composition- and symmetry-balanced dataset and used them to search 2,500 binary and ternary structure prototypes covering about one billion inorganic compounds.
Limitation / still unknown
This is an arXiv preprint and the reported stable compounds are computationally predicted, with DFT convex-hull validation; the study does not report their experimental synthesis. Stability depends on the calculated structures and thermodynamic reference data. The additional ~150,000 compounds are near-hull candidates, not counted as thermodynamically stable discoveries in the title or summary.

This is a search within a defined design space of LiPF₆ in EC/EMC/DMC solvents, not a claim that the constituent chemicals or all six electrolyte recipes were wholly unprecedented. Pouch-cell tests used nominal 220 mAh graphite‖LiNi0.5Mn0.3Co0.2O2 cells and a baseline chosen from the same design space; results do not establish commercial-scale manufacturing or long-term fleet performance. The main-table complete-data cohort comprises 307 hypertensive participants (100 primary aldosteronism, 69 pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma, 30 Cushing syndrome and 108 primary hypertension); 101 normotensive volunteers were excluded from model fitting/testing. This is an internal random holdout from expert referral centres, with small minority classes and no untouched external or prospective clinical evaluation. Comparing the best selected mono-omics and multi-omics models is study-specific, not a general guarantee of diagnostic improvement.

Editorial relevance 40 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Pretrained neural segmentation converted patient CT scans into quantitative lung features used with clinical variables in the represented mortality score; learned risk modeling and binning enabled the patient-outcome discrimination analysis.
Test and result
A multicenter first-wave dataset was reduced from 1,575 enrolled patients to 1,125 complete records, including 292 deaths. Repeated train/test splits and repeated cross-validation compared candidate models and selected a five-variable logistic model. Pretrained learned segmentation enabled automated lung measurements. A later, prospectively collected single-center cohort of 213 patients, including 31 deaths, yielded AUC 0.808 with reported 95% confidence interval 0.740–0.877.
Limitation / still unknown
Prospective cohort collection does not establish that the model and thresholds were fixed before its outcomes were known. Complete-case selection, different pandemic waves, one-center later validation and historical treatment conditions limit transportability. The paper inconsistently describes 213 versus 214 validation patients and presents four low-risk deaths as 1.8% without a clearly appropriate low-risk denominator; those percentages and post-hoc exclusions are not adopted here. Supplemental acquisition/endpoint details were not independently read. No causal CT mechanism, intervention benefit or current clinical utility is established.

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A one-dimensional convolutional network analyzed EEGs from 358 adults with acute consciousness impairment. Technology: t-VGG GAP one-dimensional convolutional neural network

Editorial relevance 33 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The CNN learned EEG features directly to classify clinical outcomes and etiologies; Grad-CAM and visual review explored model behavior without proving a new causal mechanism.
Test and result
This post-hoc analysis reused the four-hospital CERTA EEG trial. A fixed previously published CNN architecture used overlapping epochs, while stratified five-fold splitting kept all epochs from a patient together; patient predictions averaged epoch outputs. Prognosis used survival at six months and the best Cerebral Performance Category measured at four weeks or six months. All 358 patients contributed prognostic evaluation; diagnostic etiology classification used 277 eligible patients and reached 54.5% accuracy.
Limitation / still unknown
Original trial randomization concerned EEG recording strategy, not this learned model. The best-of-two-timepoints functional endpoint is not a fixed six-month recovery measure. Model-output confidence selected progressively smaller subgroups and does not establish calibrated clinical certainty; higher-confidence performance must not be reported as whole-cohort accuracy. Earlier random-forest work used the same cohort, so this is not an independent replication of its findings. Treatment decisions and withdrawal of life support may affect observed prognosis; authors argue that using the first EEG reduced but did not remove that concern. There was no held-out new hospital, prospective model-guided treatment or demonstrated patient benefit. The represented date is the documented August 2022 online journal version, without an earliest-priority assertion.

25 Aug 2022Wuhan University; Zhongnan Hospital of Wuhan University

Learned sepsis groups show different observed hospital mortality in an ICU cohort

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: K-means clustering of eleven routine first-day measurements grouped 8,817 sepsis records into two clinical patterns. Observed hospital mortality differed between groups and remained associated after statistical adjustment. This is a retrospective cohort relationship, without established biological subtypes, causal treatment effects or validated bedside deployment.

Technology: Unsupervised K-means clustering of routine ICU clinical measurements

Editorial relevance 33 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
K-means learned multivariable patient groups without using mortality as its clustering target; subsequent outcome analysis linked those learned groups to observed hospital mortality. PCA visualization alone and recovery of known individual severity markers are not the represented result.
Test and result
The source selected 8,817 MIMIC-IV sepsis patients and used eleven expert-selected variables measured during the first ICU day. It compared two-to-eight clusters and selected two using clustering criteria. Hospital mortality was 29.4% in the smaller group versus 8.5% in the larger group; adjusted odds ratio was 2.214, 95% CI 1.780–2.754. Outcome differences are actual cohort observations beyond cluster-separation scores.
Limitation / still unknown
The groups were derived and compared in the same retrospective single-center database, without external transportability testing. They may reflect severity and clinical heterogeneity rather than distinct biological entities. Missing lactate and oxygenation values required imputation; absent baseline SOFA and unmeasured infection characteristics may bias case definition and associations. No causal therapy-response difference, prospective prediction or operational benefit was shown.

Finding: A recurrent neural network generated peptide sequences and classified predicted activity and hemolysis; a genetic-algorithm route also generated analogues. After sequence and physicochemical filters, researchers synthesized and tested 33 peptides. Machine learning generates active daunomycin-binding synthetic nucleic-acid polymers outside selected sequence families

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: The study combined in-vitro selection with a conditional variational autoencoder trained on selection data to generate high-affinity highly functionalized nucleic-acid polymer (HFNAP) sequences. Experimentally generated CVAE sequences bound daunomycin with reported dissociation constants of 9–26 nM despite having no apparent primary-sequence similarity to experimentally selected polymers; competition selections found selected generated variants performed as well as or better than sequences obtained after multiple rounds of high-stringency selection.

Technology: Conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) trained on in-vitro selection-derived HFNAP sequence/fitness data

Editorial relevance 60 chemistry Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The authors used the CVAE to condition generation of novel HFNAP sequences on predicted daunomycin-binding fitness, then synthesized/tested generated sequences in binding and competition-selection assays. The machine-learning model generated the active sequences; wet-lab selection and competition assays established their binding activity.
Test and result
Experimentally generated CVAE sequences bound daunomycin with reported dissociation constants of 9–26 nM despite having no apparent primary-sequence similarity to experimentally selected polymers; competition selections found selected generated variants performed as well as or better than sequences obtained after multiple rounds of high-stringency selection.
Limitation / still unknown
The finding is target binding by synthetic HFNAPs, not therapeutic efficacy or cellular activity. Binding results are specific to daunomycin and reported assays; the authors describe sequences as having no apparent similarity rather than proving wholly unrelated functional mechanisms. Some competition performance was assessed by in-vitro selection rather than a clinical or organism-level test.

4 Aug 2022ATLAS Collaboration; CERN

ATLAS boosted decision trees enable first observation of triple-W boson production

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: In 139 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV LHC data, ATLAS observed simultaneous WWW production at 8.0σ (5.4σ expected) and measured an inclusive cross-section of 820 ± 100(stat) ± 80(syst) fb. The analysis selected same-sign dilepton-plus-jets and trilepton final states. Two boosted decision trees—one per channel—improved signal/background separation and supplied distributions for the fit. The measured rate is about 2.6σ above the Standard Model prediction, not a significant discrepancy.

Technology: Two boosted decision tree classifiers for the dilepton and trilepton channels

Editorial relevance 60 physics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The BDTs were trained separately for the two- and three-lepton channels, using 12 and 11 well-modelled event variables respectively, to discriminate WWW signal from background. Their output distributions entered the likelihood fit; the paper says the improved separation helped enable the observation.
Test and result
In 139 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV LHC data, ATLAS observed simultaneous WWW production at 8.0σ (5.4σ expected) and measured an inclusive cross-section of 820 ± 100(stat) ± 80(syst) fb.
Limitation / still unknown
The final peer-reviewed paper reports 8.0σ (5.4σ expected), superseding the earlier 2021 conference-note/press account that quoted 8.2σ and 850 fb. CMS had previously observed combined inclusive production of three massive gauge bosons; this ATLAS paper is the first observation specifically of WWW production. The measured cross-section is about 2.6σ above the theory prediction, below a significant deviation, with data-driven background and systematic uncertainties included.

1 Aug 2022University of Exeter; ETH Zurich; UK Met Office; NASA Goddard Space Flight Center; University of Cambridge; University of Leeds

Machine learning isolates aerosol-driven cloud-cover increase after the Holuhraun eruption

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Using MODIS satellite observations and a random-forest counterfactual trained on meteorology and non-eruption years, researchers estimated cloud responses to the 2014 Holuhraun volcanic aerosol plume. They found cloud fraction increased by about 10% across the studied region; this change contributed more to the estimated aerosol cooling than the smaller radiative effect from brighter clouds with smaller droplets. The study supplies an observational constraint on aerosol–cloud climate forcing.

Technology: Random-forest ML-MODIS surrogate trained on meteorological reanalysis and MODIS satellite data from 2001–2020, excluding the 2014 eruption year

Editorial relevance 53 climate Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The random forest estimated the cloud properties expected under observed meteorological conditions without volcanic aerosol, creating a counterfactual baseline. Comparing these predictions with 2014 MODIS observations let the authors isolate cloud changes associated with the Holuhraun aerosol perturbation from meteorological co-variability and estimate the relative radiative contributions of cloud-fraction, liquid-water-path, and droplet-size changes.
Test and result
Using MODIS satellite observations and a random-forest counterfactual trained on meteorology and non-eruption years, researchers estimated cloud responses to the 2014 Holuhraun volcanic aerosol plume.
Limitation / still unknown
The result concerns one volcanic natural experiment, Holuhraun in 2014, and satellite observations of a North Atlantic/Northern European region. The cloud response is estimated by comparing observations with an ML counterfactual and is not a randomized intervention; it depends on model and MODIS retrieval assumptions. The paper reports about a 10% cloud-cover increase and attributes the leading radiative contribution to cloud fraction, while the droplet-size effect is also present and the liquid-water-path contribution is weak.

Finding: A three-dimensional convolutional network distinguished 29 postanoxic-coma patients from 34 healthy volunteers using structural and functional MRI measurements. Posterior-cingulate functional connectivity provided the strongest reported internal discrimination, outperforming the tested structural inputs. The result is a small clinical imaging feasibility study, without independently validated prediction of recovery or demonstrated bedside benefit.

Technology: Custom three-dimensional convolutional neural network for multimodal brain MRI classification

Editorial relevance 33 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The trained 3D CNN learned spatial features from patient and control MRI volumes, enabling the represented clinical-status discrimination and comparison of the informative content of different MRI inputs.
Test and result
A prospectively collected single-center cohort included 29 postanoxic-coma patients and 34 healthy volunteers. Separate structural and functional MRI inputs were evaluated with a custom 3D CNN using ten-times repeated tenfold cross-validation. Input intensity normalization used training-set values. Posterior-cingulate functional-connectivity inputs achieved reported mean accuracy 0.96, versus 0.82 for T1 structural input.
Limitation / still unknown
Small groups, a healthy-control contrast, one scanner/center and repeated internal cross-validation limit clinical specificity and generalization. Prospective collection is not an external locked-model evaluation. Convolutional activation maps were derived from correctly classified training samples and do not establish causal consciousness mechanisms. Post-hoc favorable outcomes among a few misclassified patients are not independent recovery prediction. No clinical deployment, prognosis-guided intervention or outcome benefit was demonstrated.

Ground-Level NO2 Surveillance from Space Across China for High Resolution Using Interpretable Spatiotemporally Weighted Artificial Intelligence.

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: The models produced 100%-coverage daily 1-km estimates for China in 2019–2020, with out-of-sample/out-of-city R2 0.93/0.71. Analysis found average urban-rural differences of 28%, Spring Festival and National Day declines of 22% and 14%, and slower post-lockdown recovery in surface concentrations than satellite columns. Ground measurements from approximately 1,630 stations were used with out-of-sample and out-of-city cross-validation; the article reports RMSEs and spatial/temporal pattern checks. Estimates are model-derived, and the paper does not establish causal explanations for the observed urban, holiday, or pandemic patterns.

Machine-learning-guided Fe₂P-type alloys reach cryogenic magnetocaloric temperatures without rare earths

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: An artificial neural network trained on reported experimental compositions guided optimization of Fe₂P-type Mn–Fe–P–Si alloys for sub-77 K magnetocaloric use. Experiments measured a 97 K transition for Mn₁.₇₀Fe₀.₃₀P₀.₆₃Si₀.₃₇ at 1 T; replacing a small fraction of Fe with Co lowered the transition to 73 K. The Co-containing composition showed a 7.5 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ magnetic entropy change and a 1.4 K reversible adiabatic temperature change under a 0–5 T field.

Technology: Artificial neural network trained on a curated, literature-mined dataset of experimental Fe₂P-type magnetocaloric compounds

Editorial relevance 53 materials Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The team mined published experimental composition/property results to train an artificial neural network for composition optimization toward lower transition temperatures. Predictions guided selection of Mn₁.₇₀Fe₀.₃₀P₀.₆₃Si₀.₃₇, then a minor Co-for-Fe substitution was tested experimentally to reduce its transition temperature below 77 K. AI guided composition selection; the reported magnetic and caloric properties came from measurements on synthesized samples.

An artificial neural network trained on reported experimental compositions guided optimization of Fe₂P-type Mn–Fe–P–Si alloys for sub-77 K magnetocaloric use.

Finding: Unsupervised X-ray diffraction temperature clustering (X-TEC) analyzed high-volume temperature-dependent diffraction data from Cd₂Re₂O₇. The extracted selection rules indicate that Cd and Re displacements are approximately equal in amplitude and opposite in phase, revealing a previously unrecognized involvement of Re 5d electrons in the structural order. The analysis also resolves X-ray diffraction evidence for fluctuations associated with the structural transitions. This is a data-driven interpretation of measured diffraction, not a new direct imaging of atom trajectories.

Editorial relevance 53 materials Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
X-TEC clustered temperature trajectories of diffraction intensities across a high-volume reciprocal-space dataset to identify structural order parameters and weaker diffuse-scattering fluctuations. Its data-driven selection rules exposed the reciprocal-space pattern from which researchers inferred approximately equal, out-of-phase Cd and Re displacements and the Re 5d contribution; the manual crystallographic analysis would have required selecting only a small number of peaks.
Test and result
Unsupervised X-ray diffraction temperature clustering (X-TEC) analyzed high-volume temperature-dependent diffraction data from Cd₂Re₂O₇.
Limitation / still unknown
The displacement relation and Re 5d involvement are physical interpretations inferred from XRD selection rules and X-TEC clustering, not direct atom-by-atom imaging. The findings concern the analyzed crystal and temperature-dependent synchrotron diffraction data.

28 May 2022Technical University of Munich; Klinikum rechts der Isar

Neural phase-label flickering tracks atypical courses in a small surgical-video study

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Researchers found that unstable phase labels from a pretrained surgical-video network coincided with complicated or atypical courses in fifteen recorded operations. The observed pattern supplied an exploratory alert signal beyond ordinary phase-recognition accuracy. Flicker measures and thresholds were developed on the same videos, so the result does not establish an independently validated complication detector or better clinical documentation.

Technology: TeCNO convolutional temporal surgical-phase recognition with post-hoc flicker analysis

Editorial relevance 33 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The neural network generated time-ordered surgical-phase predictions; instability in those learned predictions exposed the represented association with atypical observed operative courses. The reporting interface itself is not treated as a scientific discovery.
Test and result
TeCNO was trained on 52 surgical videos and applied to fifteen further cholecystectomy videos, independently phase-annotated by a highly experienced surgeon. Investigators then reviewed unstable label clusters and derived flicker thresholds on those same fifteen cases. The source reports that threshold rules identified five of six apparently divergent courses; one gallbladder perforation produced no substantial flicker increase.
Limitation / still unknown
Post-hoc pattern recognition, same-cohort cutoff derivation and a very small event count create substantial optimism and selection risk. Independent blinded complication adjudication and external alert validation were not established. Phase-annotation agreement, report generation and exploratory event association do not demonstrate complete or safer operative documentation, real-time deployment, improved outcomes or reliable detection of specific complication types.

Global Estimation and Mapping of the Conservation Status of Tree Species Using Artificial Intelligence

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: For 21,691 unassessed tree species, the authors estimated 22,889 of 58,429 species overall (39.1%) as possibly threatened, raising coverage to 52,191 species; results highlighted differences across taxa and regions. Fivefold cross-validation on assessed species: binary classifier accuracy 83.7% (87.1% for not threatened and 78.1% for possibly threatened); 100 Monte Carlo dropout predictions characterized uncertainty. This is predictive assessment, not expert-confirmed IUCN status; higher-confidence filtering yielded 90% accuracy for fewer cases.

Technology: A supervised fully connected neural network using species occurrence, range, biome, climate and human-footprint features predicted extinction-risk categories for species without IUCN assessments.

New spectra confirmed significant changes in broad Balmer emission in four of six observed candidates, establishing new type 2-to-type 1 transitions. The other two observed objects had only tentative evidence and are not counted as confirmed transitions.

Technology: ALeRCE light-curve classifier (hierarchical imbalanced random forest)

Editorial relevance 53 astronomy Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The ALeRCE random-forest classifier used variability features from ZTF light curves and ZTF/AllWISE photometric colors to classify alert sources as AGN-like. Its classifications were cross-matched against a pre-existing spectroscopic type-2 AGN sample to produce candidates with current type-1-like variability; this AI-assisted shortlist enabled follow-up spectroscopy that confirmed the transitions.
Test and result
A hierarchical random-forest classifier in the ALeRCE broker applied to Zwicky Transient Facility alert-stream light curves helped select candidate changing-look active galactic nuclei from objects previously classified as type 2.
Limitation / still unknown
Only six of the 30 visually retained candidates received new spectra in this paper, selected partly for observability; four showed clear >3σ broad-line changes and two were tentative. Thus the reported ≥66% success rate is a small, selected follow-up sample, not an unbiased prevalence estimate. The authors note possible 30–50% misclassification in the parent type-2 sample and that the ZTF alert threshold makes the method incomplete.

Active-learning experiments reveal distinct on-field and off-field polarization-switching behavior in ferroelectrics

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: An active-learning workflow paired with automated piezoresponse-force microscopy discovered relationships between local ferroelectric domain structure and polarization-switching hysteresis. The experimentally selected sampling paths and points differed substantially between on-field and off-field hysteresis loops, indicating that the two measurement modes are dominated by different mechanisms. The reference is a deformably registered planning image, not an independently measured true delivered patient dose. GAN models learned joint species-presence distributions from 5153 recorded vegetation patches. Generated composition abundance and soil-affinity patterns were compared with the observed data; higher-order conditional association estimates were derived from generated configurations.
Limitation / still unknown
The specific third- and fourth-order conditional frequencies were not independently checked in held-out field data. Generated patches and repeated model initializations are not independent field replication. Co-occurrence does not prove competition, facilitation or other mechanisms. VAE-generated succession, pioneer rankings and restoration benefits are outside this record; reconstruction accuracy is not ecological forecast accuracy.

Finding: A bidirectional LSTM classifier was evaluated for readmission using records from 4,336 colorectal-surgery patients. The source reports internal discrimination with an 80:20 training/test split, using perioperative and postoperative information. The result is a retrospective clinical model evaluation, without established preoperative prediction, external validation or demonstrated benefit from changing surgical care.

Technology: Bidirectional LSTM classifier applied to reshaped clinical patient records

Editorial relevance 33 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The learned classifier combined clinical-record features to discriminate observed readmission labels, supplying the represented retrospective outcome-evaluation result. Conventional descriptive associations with surgical approaches are not attributed to AI discovery.
Test and result
A prospectively maintained surgical database covered 4,336 operations during 2003–2019, including 321 readmissions. The paper compared multiple classifiers and describes an 80:20 split for readmission analysis. Its three-hidden-layer bidirectional LSTM reportedly achieved sensitivity 84.1% and specificity 90.9%. Predictor candidates included clinical, operative and postoperative variables; a reduced set retained length of stay and operative details.
Limitation / still unknown
Prospective database maintenance does not make model evaluation prospective. Feature selection and preprocessing isolation from testing are incompletely specified, and no external or temporal test was reported. Inclusion of postoperative variables prevents a preoperative risk claim; the permissible prediction time and all-variable leakage risks are not fully established. The reported 87.5% accuracy equals the mean of reported sensitivity and specificity, so it is not adopted as an authenticated population-weighted accuracy. Reshaping records for LSTM does not establish genuine longitudinal sequence learning. No causal effect of surgical approach or improvement in care was tested.

24 Jan 2022University of Arizona

Recurrent networks classify cancer-bearing mouse ovary images

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A convolutional LSTM classified optical-coherence tomography of excised ovaries from sixteen mice, half from an ovarian-cancer model and half wild-type controls. Tissue pathology supported the disease labels. Across repeated leave-one-animal-out evaluations, mean AUC was 0.81; the best run reached 0.98. This is a small retrospective preclinical imaging validation, not human ovarian-cancer screening or evidence of earlier detection or improved treatment outcomes.

Technology: Convolutional long short-term memory; VGG and three-dimensional CNN comparisons

Editorial relevance 33 medicine Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The convolutional LSTM learns sequential relationships between depth-resolved OCT slices and classifies tissue from cancer-model versus wild-type animals, using pathology-supported labels.
Test and result
Existing ex-vivo ovarian OCT recordings from eight cancer-model and eight wild-type mice, with pathological verification and leave-one-animal-out testing repeated ten times. Mean convolutional-LSTM AUC .81 is distinguished from the selected peak .98.
Limitation / still unknown
Human diagnostic transfer, clinical screening, early-stage detection and benefit remain unestablished. Only sixteen animals and one held-out animal per fold limit uncertainty estimates; peak-run performance is not representative average performance.
